doc.title: Fred Radke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Hillsdale, Michigan, November 8, 2023

title: Repertoire, one-nighters, Harry's love of sports, and Bill Muncie
summary: The band's modern tunes and singers, the tour, leaving being hard, and Harry's fondness for hydroplane driver Bill Muncie.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: How did he deal with the ever-changing musical tastes?

We did, you know we were doing some Blood, Sweat & Tears things. He always had a good singer too, on the band, a female singer. Really good, except once. That sounds pretty funny. But no, he always had a dynamite singer and he tried to do some modern things. We did like “Traces” and he did “Spinning Wheel” and he did things like that. We spent a lot of time in Vegas because that’s where his home was. And we’d go out — I never really went — he never went out like we did with the Fiftieth Anniversary. We did four months of one-nighters off a bus, you were talking about that. And that’s brutal but it is what it is. And most of the guys who were on the band would stay on the band. And some guys would jump. But when I left the band it was the most difficult thing I think that — one of the most difficult things that I had to do, because it was a job that I loved. I could hardly wait to get on the bandstand, I was so thrilled. And he knew that. He could tell. And then I knew Harry, we had social friends. I knew him — we had mutual friends socially. Like he was a real sports guy. If a famous musician walked into the room and a famous baseball player or a sports figure, he would gravitate to the sports figure before he would to the musician. Okay? Well my very dear friend that took my place when I went with the band as Gina’s conductor was Bill Muncie. And Bill Muncie was the world’s —

still is, gone now — world’s greatest unlimited hydroplane driver. I mean he hit — won more gold cups, anything, world records, 67 victories, and Harry was a fan of his. And so he’d come up and he said, “What happened to Bill today in Detroit? What did he say?” And then Bill came by to see me a few times with the band. And so see it was on a different level. And then he loved Corky. Corky was his adopted son you know that don’t you?
